# Final report

## Outcome

The submitted edit changes only the last layer (`fc.weight`, `fc.bias`). On the practice images it raises worst-group accuracy from 72.9% to 90.8% while the weighted mean goes from 97.7% to 95.4%. Both targets are met on practice, but the cushion is thin, and on the harder half of the practice set the weighted mean alone is 93.1%, below the 94% line.

| | landbird/land | landbird/water | waterbird/land | waterbird/water | worst | weighted mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original | 99.4 | 82.6 | 72.9 | 96.2 | 72.9 | 97.7 |
| **Submitted edit** (pass 10) | 96.4 | 90.8 | 93.2 | 93.2 | **90.8** | **95.4** |
| Paired change (fixed / broken) | 0 / 14 | 41 / 3 | 27 / 0 | 0 / 4 | | |
| Out-of-sample estimate (cross-fitted halves) | 97.2 | 89.9 | 92.5 | 94.0 | 89.9 | 96.2 |

The cross-fitted row scores each image with a version of the recipe whose statistics did not use that image.

## What I changed

With `wd = W[1] − W[0]` the readout the decision depends on:

- **Background cancellation.** `W[1] −= (λ/2)·d_p⊥` and `W[0] += (λ/2)·d_p⊥`, with λ = 0.2487.
  - `d_p` is the water-minus-land difference of group-mean `avgpool` features, averaged within bird class.
  - `d_y` is the waterbird-minus-landbird difference, averaged within background.
  - `d_p⊥` is the part of `d_p` orthogonal to `d_y`, i.e. a background coordinate with zero mean response to the bird.
  - λ = (wd·d_p)/‖d_p⊥‖² is the one strength at which the new readout has zero projection on `d_p` and an unchanged projection on `d_y`.
- **Bias.** The margin offset is set to `λ·d_p⊥·c + 1.196`.
  - `c` is the mean of the four group means, so a background-neutral image keeps its margin.
  - 1.196 = log(0.7679/0.2321) removes the class prior of the fine-tuning data. I fixed this before the first edited pass.

Nothing was fitted: every number comes from group means, the original weights, or the stated training shares.

## What goes wrong in the network

- **Size of the shortcut.** The bird moves the margin by about 16 units and the background by about 8, against a within-group spread of about 5.
- **Background alone drives the output.** On bird-free collages built from image corners, water backgrounds score 9.4 units higher than land, and 73% are called "waterbird" with no bird present (0% for land). The same bird patch pasted into a water surround scores 6.7 units higher than in a land surround, in all 32 cases.
- **Shared axis.** In the features the last layer reads, the background shifts activations along nearly the same axis as the bird (cosine 0.57 between `d_p` and `d_y`).
- **Not a few channels.** The 10 channels contributing most to the background effect supply 0.93 of 8.08 units and carry as much bird evidence. This ruled out channel ablation.
- **Depth.** Bird and background directions are orthogonal at `layer3` (cosine 0.04) and `layer4.0` (0.08), and merge in `layer4.1` (0.30) and `layer4.2` (0.57).

## Causal evidence

**Dose-response on the last-layer direction** (four real passes, half-A statistics):

| Strength | LL | LW | WL | WW | Background effect on mean margin | Swap surround effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (original) | 99.4 | 82.6 | 72.9 | 96.2 | +8.08 | +6.67 |
| 0.5 | 98.7 | 85.6 | 88.0 | 94.7 | +4.21 | +3.31 |
| 1 | 97.2 | 90.1 | 93.2 | 94.0 | +0.34 | −0.04 |
| 2 | 80.9 | 95.7 | 98.5 | 86.5 | −7.39 | −6.75 |

Strength 2 reverses the bias, so the formerly favoured groups become the weak ones. Strengths 0.5 to 2 also carry the prior correction; strength 0 is the untouched model.

**The two components separately.** The direction edit alone (pass 8) gives 98.5 / 92.9 / 91.0 / 92.5, so it is the repair. The prior correction only trades landbird accuracy (−2.8, −1.3 points) for waterbird accuracy (+2.3, +1.5). I kept it because the waterbird groups are measured on only 133 images each and need the slack.

**Held-out checks.**
- Statistics from half A, tested on half B: worst group 68.7 → 89.3%, with the same gains as on half A.
- Statistics from half B alone (pass 9) reproduce the repair; the two recipes disagree on 14 of 1,199 predictions.
- The stimuli played no part in building the edit.

**Upstream localisation** (three passes at the `layer3`→`layer4` boundary, last layer original):
- Erasing one place direction there removes 81% of the mean background effect (8.08 → 1.56) with the bird effect intact. I had predicted only a modest effect, so that prediction was wrong.
- It is a worse repair, though: within-group spread rises and worst group reaches only 85.7%.
- Erasing 16 background directions, or the 15 non-place ones, also falls short. A last-layer correction on those features is predicted at d′ 3.28, against 3.41 on the original features.
- So the shortcut's input enters through a low-dimensional part of `layer3`, but the repair belongs at the last layer.

## Limits you should know

- **Ceiling from the data, as far as I can tell.** Several remaining landbird/water errors have real ducks, spoonbills or geese in the background photo. Several "waterbird" errors look like flycatchers and a towhee; I believe this comes from name-matching when the dataset was built, but I have no species labels to confirm it.
- **Risk on the test set.** My rough estimate of meeting both targets is 80–90%. The final version differs from the half-A version (pass 2, kept in `work/best_1`) on 10 images: 4 more landbird/land errors and 3 fewer landbird/water errors. That gives it more cushion on the worst group and less on the mean; I kept it as planned because the two are equivalent within uncertainty.
- **How predictions were made.** I predicted group means and spreads of edited margins from group means and covariances, never per-image outputs. Those predictions matched every pass exactly. All accuracies quoted come from forward passes, except the cross-fitted row, which combines the per-image predictions of passes 2 and 9.

All 10 passes are used. `work/edited` holds the two submitted tensors, with a copy in `work/best_final`; the full log is in `work/notes.md`.
